items.title: Percentage of households with internet access in one country, 2010 to 2022
points: The line graph shows the percentage of households with internet access in one country between 2010 and 2022.
Access rose every period, from 38% in 2010 to 91% in 2022, so it more than doubled over twelve years.
The sharpest increase came between 2016 and 2018, when the figure jumped from 64% to 79%.
After 2020 growth slowed noticeably, with only a three point rise from 88% to 91%.
Overall, internet access became almost universal, although the pace of growth levelled off at the end of the period.

items.title: Average monthly temperature in a coastal town, January to December
points: The graph illustrates the average monthly temperature in a coastal town over the course of a year.
January was the coldest month at 4°C, after which temperatures climbed steadily through the spring.
The peak came in July at 21°C, with August only slightly lower at 20°C.
From September temperatures fell sharply, dropping from 17°C to 5°C by December.
In summary, the town has a clear seasonal pattern, with a range of 17 degrees between the coldest and warmest months.

items.title: Birth rate in one country, 1970 to 2020
points: The line graph shows the number of births per 1,000 people in one country from 1970 to 2020.
The birth rate fell in every decade, from 28 in 1970 to 11 in 2020, which is a drop of more than half.
The steepest decline was between 1980 and 1990, when it fell from 24 to 19.
The decrease slowed in the final decade, with the rate easing from 13 to 11.
Overall, the country experienced a long and steady fall in its birth rate, reaching its lowest point in 2020.

items.title: Cars per 100 households in urban and rural areas of one country, 1995 to 2020
points: The graph compares car ownership, measured as cars per 100 households, in urban and rural areas of one country between 1995 and 2020.
In urban areas ownership rose from 62 to a peak of 68 in 2005, then declined to 58 by 2020.
Rural ownership, by contrast, grew throughout the period, from 48 in 1995 to 84 in 2020.
The two lines crossed between 2005 and 2010, when rural households overtook urban ones.
Overall, car ownership moved in opposite directions, and by 2020 rural households owned 26 more cars per 100 households than urban ones.

items.title: Carbon dioxide emissions per person in Country A and Country B, 1990 to 2020
points: The line graph shows carbon dioxide emissions per person, in tonnes, in two countries from 1990 to 2020.
Country A's emissions rose slightly to a peak of 12.1 tonnes in 2000 and then fell steadily to 7.6 tonnes in 2020.
Country B's emissions increased in every period, almost quadrupling from 2.1 tonnes in 1990 to 8.1 tonnes in 2020.
The two lines crossed between 2015 and 2020, when Country B overtook Country A.
In conclusion, the countries followed opposite trends, and the large gap of 9.1 tonnes in 1990 had been reversed by the end of the period.

items.title: Annual visitors to a museum and a science centre in one city, 2016 to 2023
points: The graph shows the number of annual visitors to a museum and a science centre in one city between 2016 and 2023.
Both attractions grew steadily until 2019, when the museum had 470 thousand visitors and the science centre 380 thousand.
In 2020 numbers collapsed at both, falling to 120 thousand at the museum and 90 thousand at the science centre.
The science centre recovered faster, overtaking the museum in 2021 and staying ahead in 2022 with 400 thousand against 390 thousand.
By 2023 the museum was ahead again at a record 480 thousand, while the science centre also reached its highest figure of 450 thousand.

items.title: Average auction price of coffee and tea per kilogram, 2015 to 2023
points: The line graph compares the average auction price of a kilogram of coffee and tea from 2015 to 2023.
Coffee started higher at 3.2 dollars but drifted down to its lowest point of 2.6 dollars in 2019.
Tea was more stable, rising gradually from 2.7 dollars to 3.3 dollars with only a small dip in 2019, and it was more expensive than coffee from 2017 to 2020.
Coffee then rose sharply, overtaking tea again in 2021 and peaking at 5.3 dollars in 2022 before easing to 4.6 dollars in 2023.
Overall, tea prices were steady, while coffee prices were far more volatile and ended well above tea.

items.title: Life expectancy at birth in three regions, 1960 to 2020
points: The graph shows life expectancy at birth in three regions between 1960 and 2020.
Region A had the highest figure throughout, rising steadily from 68 years to 80 years.
Region B improved more quickly, from 52 years to 73 years, an increase of 21 years.
Region C started lowest at 41 years and dipped slightly from 51 to 50 between 1990 and 2000, but then rose sharply to 62 years by 2020.
Overall, life expectancy increased in all three regions, and the gap between Region A and Region C narrowed from 27 years to 18 years.

items.title: Number of students enrolled in three subjects at a university, 2014 to 2022
points: The line graph shows enrolment in engineering, arts and computing at one university from 2014 to 2022.
Arts was the most popular subject in 2014 with 1,800 students, but it declined steadily to 1,200 in 2022.
Engineering grew gradually from 1,200 to 1,700 students, and it drew level with arts at 1,500 in 2018 before moving ahead.
Computing showed the most dramatic change, quadrupling from 600 to 2,400 students and overtaking both other subjects between 2018 and 2020.
In conclusion, computing went from the least to the most popular subject, while arts fell from first place to last.

items.title: Value of exports from one country to four trading partners, 2000 to 2020
points: The graph shows the value of one country's exports to four trading partners between 2000 and 2020, in billions of US dollars.
Partner C was the largest market in 2000 at 15 billion, but exports to it fell steadily to 9 billion, the lowest of the four in 2020.
Exports to Partner B grew fastest, from 8 billion to 30 billion, overtaking Partner A between 2010 and 2015 to become the largest market.
Partner A rose more modestly from 12 billion to 21 billion, while Partner D grew from 3 billion to 14 billion and overtook Partner C between 2010 and 2015.
Overall, total exports to the four partners almost doubled, from 38 billion to 74 billion, with Partner C the only market to decline.
